title: The exceptional inverse image
statement:
Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$ be an admissible coefficient
ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of the standing schemes (separated and of finite type
over the standing field $k$, with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$; [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]).

1. The objects of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ ([sk-def-sfb-constructible]) are compact in
   $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ ([sk-def-localizing-closure]) and a small skeleton compactly
   generates it.
2. Compactifications define an exact functor
   $Rf_!\colon\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$, preserving direct sums and
   sending $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ (compare [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek]).
3. A single application of Brown representability gives an exact right adjoint
   $f^!\colon\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.
4. This right adjoint sends $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, so its adjunction
   restricts to $\Dctf$.

For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$ one has $\Dctf=\Dbc$, so the theorem
holds with $\Dbc$ in place of $\Dctf$. The finite ring $A$ is arbitrary; it need not be
regular or Gorenstein. The $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ cases are the integral and
rational cases with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] to each of the standing schemes and the given admissible coefficient. It asserts essential smallness of $\Dctf$, compactness of each of its objects in the ambient localizing closure, and generation by any small skeleton. This proves (1), including the size condition required by Brown representability.

By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], both $X$ and $Y$ are qcqs, since their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are separated and finite type. The $k$-morphism $f$ is itself separated and of finite type: writing $a_X=a_Y\circ f$ for the structure maps, $a_X$ is separated, so $f$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](b); $a_X$ is locally of finite type, so $f$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](f); and $X$ is quasi-compact while $Y$ is quasi-separated, so $f$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). This is the separated finite-type hypothesis on $f$ required by every cited statement below and in steps 3 and 4. Thus [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] applies to $f$ over the qcqs base $Y$ and supplies a dense compactification $f=p\circ j$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper. For this compactification, [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] states that $Rp_*j_!$ restricts to the exact, sum-preserving functor between the two localizing categories and carries $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Its qcqs hypothesis on $Y$ has just been checked. Moreover, [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] provides the canonical comparison isomorphisms between compactifications, independent of a common refinement and satisfying the identity and cocycle relations. Use the chosen compactification of the standing setting to obtain $Rf_!$; the comparisons show that it has the asserted compactification interpretation. This proves all of (2), including preservation of $\Dctf$.

For the same coefficient, morphism, and chosen compactification, [sk-prop-sf-existence] applies Brown representability to the exact coproduct-preserving functor from step 2 on the compactly generated category of step 1. Its conclusion gives the exact right adjoint $f^!$ and natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,f^!N)$ on the full localizing categories. This is (3); a single application works uniformly for all the admissible coefficients, including arbitrary finite $A$.

For finite $A$, [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] asserts precisely that the right adjoint from step 3 carries $\Dctf(Y,A)$ into $\Dctf(X,A)$ and that the adjunction restricts. For $\mathcal O_E$, [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] identifies the integral Brown right adjoint with the $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ instance of this same general right adjoint, with its adjunction. Hence [sk-thm-int-restriction] gives the required preservation and restricted adjunction for that functor. For $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [sk-thm-restriction] explicitly refers to the right adjoint of the general existence theorem and gives the same preservation and restricted adjunction. The cases $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ are the cases $\mathcal O_E$ and $E$ with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Thus (4) holds for every listed coefficient.

source.place: Finite, integral and rational restriction cases

proof.text: For the non-finite coefficients only, apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) to $X$ and $Y$, which are qcqs by step 2. It gives $\Dctf=\Dbc$ as full subcategories of the same module-object derived category, and equality of their localizing closures. Consequently the functors and adjunction already obtained give exactly the asserted $\Dbc$ version. No such equality is used for a finite nonregular $A$, so no regularity or Gorenstein hypothesis has been imposed on the finite coefficient ring.
